evan_sales: Quick one  prospect (large regional bank) wants a 72h POC. Requirements: BYOK (customer CMKs in Thales HSM), HSM-backed wrap/unwrap, 12-hour ephemeral KEK rotation, Splunk-forwarded attestation, and a documented offline key ceremony. They also want a firm cap on monthly HSM-op costs. Can we scope and pricing?

rachel_se: Feasible. Two POC models: 1) Hosted + external HSM proxy (we call their Thales endpoints), fastest to demo. 2) Dedicated in their VPC with direct HSM peering for lowest latency. For 12h rotation, use wrapped-DEK flow so no downtime.

sam_crypto: Crypto notes: 12h ephemeral KEKs fine. Flow: generate DEK in our runtime, wrap with customer CMK via PKCS#11 to Thales, store only wrapped blob. Attestation: we can emit signed receipts per wrap (include op-id, timestamp, requester) and forward to Splunk via HTTP Event Collector. Need vendor attestation from Thales for FIPS.

leo_ops: Ops checklist for POC: we need their Thales gateway IPs, client mTLS cert, PKCS#11 module version, and expected wrap qps. Networking: open outbound mTLS to their gateway and allow return traffic on ephemeral ports. We'll stand up a 72h staging cluster and enable dashboards (wrap latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, tcp retransmits).

evans_sales: They want a firm monthly cap on HSM ops. What billing options?

rachel_se: Two-pronged pricing we propose: predictable plan = monthly connector fee + included HSM-op allowance (e.g., 1M ops) + overage rate per-1k ops. Or fully usage: base per-token + per-crypto-op. For enterprise deals we often do a committed ops tier to cap spend and simplify forecasting. We'll add a one-time ceremony/onboarding fee.

sam_crypto: Perf caveat: proxying to Thales adds ~12-35ms per op depending on region and our routing. If they do synchronous wraps for every request at 1k qps, we should push Dedicated or a short-lived wrapped-prefix cache to reduce ops. Cache example: pre-wrap prefixes for common user sessions and reuse for X minutes.

leo_ops: POC runbook snippet for them to review:
```
POC runbook (72h)
1) T-3d: collect HSM gateway IPs + mTLS cert + PKCS#11 info
2) T-2d: provision staging pool + wireguard tunnel to their gateway
3) T-1d: run pkcs11 smoke: list-keys, wrap/unwarp samples
4) Day0: begin 72h soak, monitor wrap latency & errors, forward attestations to Splunk
5) Day3: deliver attestation export + post-mortem
```
Firewall snippet (customer):
```
allow tcp 198.51.100.77:443 -> 203.0.113.22:8443 (mTLS client-auth)
client-cert: /etc/keys/bank-mtls.pem
```

sam_crypto: Sample attestation JSON we can forward to Splunk (example):
```
{"op_id":"op-123","ts":"2026-03-01T12:00:00Z","action":"wrap","key_id":"cus-cmk-789","status":"ok","sig":"MEUCIQ..."}
```

nadia_legal: Legal: we'll need a Key Custody Appendix stating Redwood never has plaintext CMKs, explain attestation retention (we can retain audit receipts for X days per SOW), and define escrow retrieval process and fees. For dual-custody / third-party escrow, add chain-of-custody and witness requirements. Also confirm regulatory controls (FIPS 140-2/3 certs) from Thales.

evans_sales: They also asked: what happens if we lose access to their HSM during rotation window? Emergency restore path?

sam_crypto: Emergency flow: fail open -> deny signing? No, recommended: keep a short-lived emergency unwrap path via escrowed shares (split-key) strictly controlled. For the POC we can simulate failover and document rollback steps: 1) pause new DEK issuance, 2) rely on cached wrapped-DEKs for TTL, 3) escalate to ceremony to recover shares. We'll include test case in runbook.

rachel_se: I'll draft a pricing slide with two options (committed ops cap vs per-op billing) and a one-page SOW appendix.

infra-bot: ticket created  sales/POC-3201001234-byo-thales: assignee=rachel_se; due_in=4d

evans_sales: Great. Can we have the runbook + pricing slide by EOD tomorrow? Meeting Thurs morning. Thanks team :rocket:
